title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s response to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards outlines its plans to strengthen AI governance, focusing on creating clear guidelines that promote transparency, accountability, and public trust in AI systems. It emphasizes collaboration with industry, academia, and civil society to develop robust standards, support innovation, and mitigate risks associated with AI deployment.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has issued guidelines to monitor and regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to preserve assessment integrity and fairness. The policy provides clear standards and oversight mechanisms for exam boards, teachers, and learners to ensure AI tools are transparent, unbiased, and aligned with national educational objectives.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted materials are used to train and operate artificial intelligence systems and evaluates the legal, economic, and ethical consequences of that practice. It provides policy recommendations that aim to protect creators’ rights while fostering responsible AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has replied to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on AI, acknowledging the report’s warning that complacency is not an option in the face of rapid AI growth. It outlines new regulatory steps, increased funding for research, and stronger cooperation with industry to promote safe, responsible AI development while boosting the country’s competitiveness.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the terms of reference for a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards. It also provides FAQs to clarify the committee’s scope, objectives, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee regarding the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines the organisation’s views and recommendations on how AI should be regulated and overseen.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy looks at how artificial intelligence will reshape rules for medical products, aiming to keep them safe, effective and ethically used. It explains how to put the AI White Paper’s principles—like transparency, accountability, and data protection—into practice when developing and approving medical devices and drugs.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the nation’s defence forces the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI users in the world for its size. It focuses on developing advanced AI capabilities, improving operational efficiency, and ensuring responsible and reliable use of AI technologies to support national security objectives.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will team up with transport companies and experts to make the most of AI’s benefits. It also lays out measures to control risks, ensuring AI is used safely and responsibly in the transport sector.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report outlines how copyright-protected works are being incorporated into AI training and development, in line with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It tracks progress, compliance, and the implications for both content creators and AI developers.
